prompt_text: My roof has hail damage in Denver. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can give specific company names — but to pick the best local options I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood in Denver. If you share that I’ll look up 3–5 highly rated, appropriately certified roofers near you and explain why I picked each.

Meanwhile, here’s a practical plan and exactly which types of companies to call and why — so you can start today if you prefer:

Which specific kinds of contractors to contact (call 3–4)
- A manufacturer-certified installer (example certifications: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster). Why: certifications mean they meet manufacturer standards and can offer stronger shingle warranties and better installation quality control.
- A local Denver roofer with documented hail/storm-claims experience and many positive local reviews. Why: storm experience means they understand insurance processes, emergency tarps, and local permitting/inspection requirements.
- A contractor that handles insurance claims and works regularly with adjusters (or a separate public adjuster if your claim is large or disputed). Why: they can help document damage and negotiate with your insurer; public adjusters represent your interests if you need it.
- One independent estimate from a different company (to compare pricing, scope and timeline). Why: prevents overpaying and reveals scope or repair-replace differences.

How to find and vet specific companies quickly
- Use manufacturer locators: GAF (Master Elite locator), CertainTeed, Owens Corning. Search “roofing contractor locator GAF Denver” etc. Certified contractors usually have the logos on their sites.
- Check Google Reviews and Yelp for recent storm-season feedback (look for many reviews mentioning hail, insurance, and speed).
- Check BBB for complaints and how they were handled.
- Ask for proof of Colorado roofing license (if required for the scope), general liability and workers’ comp insurance, and local references.
- Avoid “storm chasers” who canvass neighborhoods aggressively and pressure you to sign the same day.

Questions to ask each roofer (phone or on-site)
- Are you a certified installer for any shingle manufacturers? Which ones?
- How many hail/storm jobs have you done in the past 12 months in Denver?
- Do you handle insurance claims and work with adjusters? Do you use Xactimate for estimates?
- Will you provide a written, itemized estimate and scope of work? Does it include permits, tear-off, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, disposal?
- Do you provide a workmanship warranty and how long? Are manufacturer warranties transferable?
- Can you provide 3 local references and photos of recent hail repairs?
- Do you offer emergency tarping if the roof is actively leaking?

Red flags to avoid
- High-pressure tactics to sign immediately or insist you must accept “their” insurance-approved estimate.
- Only accepting cash or refusing to provide a written contract.
- No local address, lots of PO boxes, or minimal online presence/reviews.
- Requests to sign over your insurance check to them without clear documentation.

What you should do right now
1. Photograph and video the roof and any interior damage before any contractor starts work.
2. Contact your insurer to report the claim and ask about their process.
3. Arrange 3 inspections within 48–72 hours if possible (storm season urgency).
4. Don’t sign anything until you’ve compared estimates and verified credentials.

If you want, tell me your Denver ZIP code or neighborhood and I’ll return 3–5 named, highly rated local roofers (with brief reasons for each pick and links to their credentials and reviews). Which area should I search?
